token_economy
tSmall context comes from raw episodes, not compression: no write-time extraction, retrieval returns a count-capped set of verbatim turns (top_k default 10) with optional neighbour expansion, deduplicated across short- and long-term legs, plus a rolling session summary capped at about message_capacity/16 words. Profile extraction caps the existing-feature list at 50 per call and consolidates a tag once it holds 20 features. There is no token budget, so expand_context and limit directly scale context. Measured: 2,577 tokens per question (OmniMemEval); vendor claims about 80% fewer input tokens than Mem0 (4.20M vs 19.21M over 1,540 q in memory mode), agent mode roughly doubles it (8.57M).
eshort_term_memory.py:147-156; semantic_ingestion.py:86-94,379-384; common/api/spec.py:567-570; arXiv 2604.04853 Table 8 (doc); SOTA_MEMU_MEMOS_LOCOMO.md:329 (doc)
speed
tWrite: episode store, episodic index and semantic enqueue run concurrently (asyncio.gather); embeddings batched per add; no LLM on the synchronous path; summaries and profile extraction in background workers (single summary worker per session with dynamic batching; semantic poller every 2 s with backoff to 60 s). Read: short-term, long-term and profile legs run concurrently; neighbour expansion and derivative-to-episode lookups gathered in parallel; per-phase latency histograms (Prometheus). Vendor claims up to 75% faster add/search than Mem0; no absolute latency published in the repo.
emain/memmachine.py:796-822,1067-1105; episodic_memory.py:412-427; event_memory.py:165-177,295-316; blog 2025-12-01 (doc)
keep
  • Keep raw turns as ground truth and index them with zero write-time LLM calls; derive lossy layers (summary, profile) asynchronously off the hot path.
  • Contextualised retrieval: expand each hit with forward-weighted timeline neighbours and rerank the whole window, then fill a cap best-first.
  • Rolling short-term summary with a single background worker, dynamic batching and recursive halving on context-length errors.
  • Neighbour-aware profile updates (pass up to 50 existing features, emit ADD/DELETE) plus threshold-triggered consolidation that carries citations.
  • Per-phase timing histograms on encode and query, and a 4x over-fetch to survive dedup when one episode yields many segments.
avoid
  • Outside-harness collapse: 91.69 self-reported vs 73.90 on OmniMemEval, with multi-hop at 53.19; vendor scores depend on a paid reranker and skip profile memory.
  • Erasure leaves derived profile features in place after their source episode is deleted (only citation rows are removed).
  • No auth, no firewall, no redaction; scope is org/project and the default profile is one per project, so in a multi-user project every user's (and the assistant's) extracted facts merge into one profile; extraction is not role-filtered.
  • Non-transactional parallel writes to episode store, index and semantic queue (open TODO #1738) allow index/storage drift.

specialities
  • nameContextualised retrieval with window reranking
    tEach vector hit becomes a nucleus expanded with timeline neighbours (1/3 back, 2/3 forward); the reranker scores the whole window as one string, and windows are unified best-first under an episode cap, trimming by forward-weighted proximity to the nucleus.
    edeclarative_memory.py:398-441,616-683; long_term_memory.py:647-700 (read)
    phaseread
  • nameZero-LLM write path over verbatim episodes
    tThe synchronous add stores the raw message and its embedding only; summaries and profile extraction run in background workers, so ingest cost is embeddings and every derived layer can be rebuilt from ground truth.
    emain/memmachine.py:796-822; event_memory.py:234-292; semantic_memory.py:806-862 (read)
    phasewrite
  • nameCombined sufficiency-and-rewrite retrieval agent
    tAn LLM router picks ChainOfQuery, SplitQuery or direct search; CoQ does the sufficiency check, evidence selection and next-hop rewrite in one call per round, accumulates evidence, stops at confidence 0.8 or 3 rounds, then reranks against all queries used.
    eretrieval_agent/agents/tool_select_agent.py:144-197; coq_agent.py:139-140,197-261,312-357 (read)
    phaserank
  • nameIncarnation-scoped tenant keys
    tSegment data is keyed by a per-incarnation UUID decoupled from the registry, making tenant deletion an O(1) registry write with asynchronous purge; adopted after measured Postgres partition-lock blow-ups (HTTP 500 at 128-way concurrency).
    esqlalchemy_segment_store.py:182-249; design/segment_store_shared_tables.md:1-20 (read)
    phasearch
  • nameLength-weighted chunk-averaged embeddings
    tInputs longer than the embedder limit are split greedily and their chunk vectors averaged by length, with requests packed to provider caps; no silent truncation of long turns.
    ecommon/embedder/openai_embedder.py:140-160,200 (read)
    phaseindex
  • nameNeighbour-aware profile with cited consolidation
    tProfile updates show the LLM up to 50 existing features and take ADD/DELETE commands; once a tag holds 20 features an LLM merges them, keeps the union of source-episode citations and is not allowed to change the tag.
    esemantic_ingestion.py:86-94,225-269,348-403,466-544 (read)
    phasederive
  • nameSelf-healing rolling summariser
    tA single background worker drains a dynamic batch into the rolling summary; on context-window errors it halves the batch, or splits a single oversize episode at its midpoint, recursively, so no turn is dropped.
    eshort_term_memory.py:468-553,594-679 (read)
    phasederive

token_economy
tSmall context is achieved mainly by (1) token-denominated recall: rank-ordered packing to max_tokens (default 4,096; doc recommends 2,048 for chatbots), metadata free; (2) consolidation: many raw facts collapse into one evidence-backed observation, with prefer_observations dropping the raw facts an observation already covers; (3) mental models: precomputed answers read with no retrieval or LLM; (4) narrative facts that carry who/when/where/why so fewer facts answer a question; (5) chunks and source facts off by default; (6) recall has no LLM call at all; (7) provider prompt caching of a bank-agnostic system prefix (missions sit in the user turn), with Anthropic, Gemini and OpenAI/xAI cache wiring; (8) reflect prompt compaction (short id aliases, minute timestamps, already-shown items by alias, oldest tool results blanked near the cap); (9) an IDF-aware cap of 16 keyword terms. Measured context per LoCoMo question is about 36k on the vendor run and 24,683 on OmniMemEval (both from our notes), far above the 4k default, so the headline scores use a much larger budget than the default.
eengine/fact_budget.py; api/http.py:517-528; config.py:1702,1925,1937-1939; docs/developer/retrieval.md [read]; engine/reflect/presentation.py; engine/cache_affinity.py; engine/search/bm25_term_selection.py [read]
speed
tRead-optimised by design: all LLM work happens at write or in the background. Recall runs four SQL arms in parallel per fact type (4 DB connections per recall), with no LLM; vendor latency is 100-600 ms recall (CPU reranker is the bottleneck; length-bucket batching is 36-54% faster; FP16 on MPS 27-36% faster), 800-3,000 ms reflect, and 500-2,000 ms per retain batch. Writes can be async (Postgres queue, SKIP LOCKED workers, auto-split into sub-batches of ~10k tokens processed concurrently), use the provider Batch API, an embedding coalescer, and consolidation of 8 facts per call with configurable parallelism. Further: queued retains to one document are folded at claim time (up to 16), each recall has a 4-connection budget, the ANN scan resumes iteratively, dateparser's language detector is rewritten, and length-bucket batching and FP16 for the local reranker are opt-in.
edocs/developer/performance.md [doc]; config.py:1293,1599,1694,1701,1759,1765; engine/retain/embedding_coalescer.py; worker/poller.py [read]; engine/retain/fold.py; engine/db_budget.py; engine/temporal_language_detection.py; config.py:1292-1293,1455 [read]
keep
  • Recall has no LLM: four cheap parallel arms (vector, lexical, one-hop link graph, dateparser temporal window) + RRF k=60 + a small local cross-encoder over 300 candidates, then bounded multiplicative boosts (recency, temporal proximity, proof count; at most about +27% / -17% combined).
  • Budget the context in tokens, not top-k, and keep 'search depth' as a separate knob; pack in rank order so one long item cannot evict shorter ones.
  • Layered read hierarchy for synthesis: mental models (precomputed, no LLM) then observations (consolidated, with proof counts and staleness flags) then raw facts as ground truth, with prefer_observations deduplicating by provenance.
  • Do contradiction handling in background consolidation over observations (create/update/delete with history, 'never compute numbers', cascade state changes) and keep raw facts append-only, so the write path stays a single extraction call per chunk.
  • Speaker-based world/experience routing at extraction, driven by caller context, and the event date in every extraction prompt so relative dates resolve at write time.
avoid
  • Benchmark opacity: the 92 LoCoMo leaderboard names no reader, judge or context; the paper's LoCoMo token budget is a literal '<add> tokens' placeholder; the vendor run reportedly uses a ~36k context and a 'be generous' judge, against a 4k default; an outside harness gets 81.99.
  • Architecture drift from the paper: opinion rows were deleted in 2026-01 and the opinion fact type and confidence column dropped in 2026-04; the entity-summary 'observation' network was replaced by mental models, so the four-network claim describes neither the current code nor the old one.
  • The write firewall is only secrets/PII regex and off by default; no injection or poisoning defence in OSS, no auth by default, and no per-writer trust on shared banks.
  • No automatic fact-level dedup or invalidation at write and no forgetting: raw facts grow without bound (only manual curation retires them), and correctness of 'current state' depends on the asynchronous consolidation having caught up (reflect must re-verify stale observations).

specialities
  • nameLLM-free recall with bounded boosts
    tRecall runs vector, keyword, one-hop graph and temporal arms in parallel per fact type, fuses by RRF and reranks with a small local cross-encoder; recency, temporal proximity and proof count can only nudge the score multiplicatively (about +27% / -17%), never override relevance.
    eengine/memory_engine.py:8804-8812; engine/search/fusion.py:29; engine/search/reranking.py:174-303 [read]
    phaserank
  • nameDrift-proof structured mental models
    tIn delta mode a mental model is a tree of sections and blocks; the refresh LLM emits operations against ids and untouched blocks are copied byte for byte, so prose drift on unchanged content is structurally impossible. Citations whose facts were invalidated or deleted are pruned.
    eengine/reflect/structured_doc.py:1-20; engine/reflect/delta_ops.py:1-25; engine/reflect/retractions.py:1-20 [read]
    phasederive
  • nameReflect prompt compaction
    tEach reflect replaces UUIDs with short aliases, trims timestamps to the minute, drops constant fields and lists already-seen items by alias, then resolves aliases back before anything is stored; UUIDs the model was never shown are scrubbed as unverified.
    eengine/reflect/presentation.py:1-60 [read]
    phaserank
  • nameBank-agnostic cached system prefix
    tRetain and consolidation missions go into the variable user turn, so one provider-side cached system prefix serves every bank; caching is wired per provider (Anthropic breakpoints, Gemini CachedContent, OpenAI/xAI affinity hints).
    eengine/retain/fact_extraction.py:1825-1830; engine/prompt_preview.py:4-9; engine/cache_affinity.py:1-24; config.py:1702 [read]
    phasecost
  • nameConsolidation rules for state change
    tObservation consolidation is told to keep one facet per observation, cascade a state change to every affected observation, keep history, delete only when superseded and never compute numbers; near-duplicates at cosine >= 0.97 get a separate one-by-one LLM verdict.
    eengine/consolidation/prompts.py:37-55; engine/consolidation/consolidator.py:151-207,282; config.py:1764 [read]
    phasetime
  • nameTemporal arm by similarity with window coverage
    tTemporal retrieval ranks in-window facts by similarity, not recency, and spreads entry points across 8 time buckets so a single dense date cannot crowd out the rest of the window.
    eengine/memories/pg/recall.py:309-371,445-463 [read]
    phaseread
  • nameIDF-aware keyword cap from pg_stats
    tLong keyword queries keep the 16 rarest terms using document frequencies that Postgres ANALYZE already maintains, with no new index or table.
    eengine/search/bm25_term_selection.py:1-30; config.py:1328-1339 [read]
    phaseindex
  • nameRetain folding at claim time
    tQueued appends to one document are folded into a single execution under the claim lock without rewriting payloads, so buffered bursts cost one re-read and one extraction pass; correctness does not depend on it.
    eengine/retain/fold.py:1-37 [read]
    phasewrite

token_economy
tSix mechanisms: (1) topic extraction compresses the conversation to a short ';'-separated keyword string before retrieval; (2) each typed list is capped at 10 items (MAX_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT_IN_SYSTEM) and episodic rows are shown as timestamp + summary + '(Details: N Characters)', so verbose details are fetched only on demand via check tools; (3) procedural skills are never broadcast into prompts, only fetched by search; (4) memory agents' chat history is wiped after each update and agent context is summarised at 75% pressure down to 10% (keep last 5); (5) 'task' sessions skip inline extraction entirely; (6) the experience distiller caps each transcript at 80,000 chars (head+tail) and each turn at 8,000. Core blocks are capped at 5,000 chars each and always injected. Paper storage claim: 15.89 MB SQLite versus 15.07 GB raw screenshots (99.9% less). No tokens-per-question figure published.
emirix/agent/agent.py:1786-2093, 1955-1968 [read]; mirix/constants.py:102, 232-233, 264, 399-411 [read]; mirix/settings.py:39-50 [read]; mirix/functions/function_sets/memory_tools.py:1743-1755 [read]; arXiv 2507.07957 Table 1 [doc]
speed
tAsync-native stack (asyncpg, redis.asyncio, aiokafka, httpx). Write is queued and returns immediately; sub-agents for different memory types run concurrently; worker pool partitioned by user_id hash (default 1 worker). Skill distillation runs fire-and-forget and distils sessions in parallel. /memory/search over all types runs concurrently and embeds the query once; /memory/retrieve/conversation is sequential and BM25-only. Optional Redis cache. Paper uses Gemini for async image upload. No latency numbers published on main; the graph_revision RESULTS.md reports 12.8 s/chunk ingest flat, 61.6 s with graph, and about 1 h QA for 1,540 questions.

keep
  • A cheap router call that picks which typed extractors run per batch, then runs them in parallel with small type-specific prompts and toolsets.
  • Active retrieval: one small-model call that outputs topics plus a temporal phrase, the phrase resolved to a date range by a rule-based parser, not the LLM.
  • Pointer-style context: show a summary plus details length, keep IDs only for the owning writer, and fetch details on demand.
  • Skills as a retrieval target, not ambient context, plus routing of task versus conversation sessions to different consolidation paths.
  • Neighbour-aware writes: each extractor sees the top-k existing rows of its own type with IDs, so it can merge or replace instead of appending.
avoid
  • Destructive LLM merges and replaces with no version history or link back to source turns; raw turns are not kept by default, so errors cannot be audited or re-derived.
  • Knowledge Vault stores credentials in a plain-text column, /memory/search returns secret_value unfiltered, the retrieve path skips scopes, and memory endpoints accept a bare x-client-id header without an API key.
  • Queued /memory/add returns before durability (in-process queue by default), and one failing sub-agent fails the whole fan-out.
  • Main's LoCoMo harness carries dataset-specific examples in its ingest and answer prompts (the vendor later flagged pre-August numbers as contaminated); the 4,096-d padding blocks ANN indexing.

specialities
  • nameTyped memory managers behind a router
    tA meta memory manager LLM picks which of five type-specialised agents (core, episodic, semantic, resource, knowledge vault) handle a batch, and they run concurrently, each with its own prompt and narrow tool set. Few engines split write-time extraction by memory type this way.
    emirix/functions/function_sets/memory_tools.py:1613-2012 [read]; mirix/prompts/system/base/meta_memory_agent.txt [read]
    phasewrite
  • namePointer-style prompt context
    tPrompt listings show each event as timestamp + summary + '(Details: N Characters)'; only the owning agent sees row IDs, and full details come through check tools on demand. This keeps neighbour context cheap without hiding that more text exists.
    emirix/agent/agent.py:1882-1925 [read]; mirix/functions/function_sets/memory_tools.py:311-345 [read]
    phaseanswer
  • nameAdaptive task/conversation routing
    tA per-session session_tag sends tool-use 'task' sessions only to skill distillation (no inline extraction calls) and 'conversation' sessions only to typed extraction, so each kind of session pays for the memory it actually uses.
    emirix/functions/function_sets/memory_tools.py:1662-1766 [read]; mirix/constants.py:311-330 [read]
    phasewrite
  • nameBudgeted skill self-evolution with lineage
    tSealed sessions are distilled into worth_learning / worth_avoiding experiences with importance, credibility and an evidence quote; a curator then edits skills under a count-driven budget (max 6), a per-edit size gate (800 chars or 0.4 change ratio), semver patch bumps and soft-delete only, recording which experiences influenced which skills.
    emirix/constants.py:332-381 [read]; mirix/functions/function_sets/memory_tools.py:479-1088 [read]; mirix/services/skill_experience_curator.py:1-28, 377-416 [read]; mirix/orm/skill_experience.py:64-108 [read]
    phasederive
  • nameExactly-once background trigger
    tThe every-5-session procedural trigger is claimed through a persisted cursor row under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and dream runs hold a Postgres advisory lock, so multi-worker deployments neither double-fire nor skip a window.
    emirix/services/agent_trigger_state_manager.py:25-30, 87-93, 168 [read]; mirix/services/auto_dream_manager.py:56-147 [read]
    phasederive
  • nameLLM phrase, rule-based dates
    tRead-time topic extraction is a forced tool call returning topics and a temporal phrase; the phrase is turned into a date range by a deterministic parser rather than by the model, then filters episodic occurred_at.
    emirix/server/rest_api.py:419-552, 2996-3044 [read]; mirix/temporal/temporal_parser.py:38-135 [read]
    phaseread
  • nameSensitivity-labelled knowledge vault
    tA dedicated store for credentials and reference values carries a low/medium/high sensitivity label; high items are withheld from every non-vault agent's prompt. The idea is unusual, though the column is unencrypted and search does not apply the filter.
    emirix/orm/knowledge_vault.py:59-78 [read]; mirix/agent/agent.py:1844-1870 [read]
    phasetrust

token_economy
tWeak by design on the graph path. No context budget, truncation or compression at answer time; GRAPH_COMPLETION inlines whole chunk texts for any chunk node on a retrieved triplet, and chunks default to about 8K tokens (min of embedding limit and half LLM output limit), giving 32,532 tokens per LoCoMo question in OmniMemEval (versus 1,862 for Zep and about 5K for MemOS). Mitigations that exist: top-k caps (5 by default; OmniMemEval used 20), chunk summaries as a separate retrievable layer (SUMMARIES, GRAPH_SUMMARY_COMPLETION), global-context prelude, explicit chunk_size, summary_method='from_extraction' to halve write calls, and dedup of nodes in the rendered context. Prompt caching not found.
edoc: OmniMemEval results.md; read: resolve_edges_to_text.py:32-106; cognee/infrastructure/llm/utils.py:14-63; graph_completion_retriever.py:62
speed
tWrite: chunks processed in batches (chunks_per_batch default 2,000) with extraction and summary calls fired concurrently via asyncio.gather; data_per_batch 20 items; incremental loading skips processed items; run_in_background; optional LLM rate limiter (60 rpm default when on, 10 for local); distributed Modal runner (distributed/). Embedding in batches of 36, at most 150 points in flight; per-row source-ref writes in one statement (measured 8x faster on the default backend, code comment). Read: hybrid lanes fetched concurrently, temporal interval extraction concurrent with candidate fetch, session turn analysis concurrent with the answer, session search concurrent, graph warm-up, zero-LLM router. No published latency numbers found.

keep
  • A rule-based, zero-LLM query router (date-scoped questions to a temporal rerank, rest to hybrid) is cheap routing worth copying.
  • Pair each chunk with an LLM summary and fuse chunk-vector and summary-vector ranks with RRF: a second, compact layer at no read cost.
  • Contradictions as explicit edges: non-destructive 'contradicts' and 'superseded_by' tags, supersede only for declared single-valued relations (maps to our coexist / contest / supersede).
  • Session cache as a fast tier with a debounced background bridge into the long-term graph (improve) is a clean multi-layer write path.
  • Normalised Timestamp leaf nodes with {verb}_at edges plus per-document date hints give strong temporal scores (81.83 on LoCoMo T) without bi-temporal machinery.
avoid
  • No context budget: inlining full ~8K-token chunks for every chunk-touching triplet yields ~32.5K tokens per question.
  • Name-only entity identity (lower-cased name) silently merges homonyms across the store and splits aliases unless an opt-in consolidation pass runs.
  • No write firewall and no trust score; contradiction checking and provenance tracking are off by default.
  • Vendor LoCoMo number (90.7) uses a non-standard question set (cat 5 in, open-domain and 143 golds out), so it is not comparable.

token_economy
tPer-turn context: up to recall_facts_limit=5 facts (relevance threshold 0.1), each a short triple-like sentence with a date, plus the deduplicated conversation summaries those facts came from, appended to the system prompt. Compression happens at write time (closed hosted extractor turns exchanges into triples and a rolling summary); there is no read-time budget, truncation or compression. Vendor-measured added context: 1,294 tokens (paper), then 721 (docs). Two things work against this: (a) BYODB prepends every stored message of the current conversation as history, and the conversation lasts the whole session (the 30-min rollover never fires because of UNIQUE(session_id)), and (b) the independent cloud run measured 8,139 tokens, which suggests the cloud recall also returns conversation messages. Write side: on the Python fallback path the extractor sees summary + last exchange only (the Rust default sends the call's own messages, usually just the new exchange because history is injected by Memori and excluded from capture), and exact-hash dedup collapses repeated facts.

speed
tWrite: the raw turn is committed synchronously after the LLM response. Augmentation is async: BYODB default is a Rust tokio worker (512-slot queue, concurrency 2, one worker thread, fed from a 15-thread Python executor; 5 retries with exponential backoff); the Python fallback is an asyncio runtime with a semaphore of 50 plus a single batch-writer thread (100 per batch, 0.1 s window, 1,000-slot queue, drop on full). Augmentation HTTP timeout is 5 s in Python and 30 s in Rust. Recall and history injection run synchronously on the caller's thread before every LLM call. Read: no LLM; one local MiniLM embedding (Rust fastembed), brute-force cosine over at most 1,000 BLOBs, BM25 over at most 50 candidates, partial sort in Rust. No published latency numbers found.

keep
  • Facts as the index, summaries as the payload: retrieve small facts, then attach their source episode summary via a mention table (cheap multi-layer context).
  • Write-time incremental extraction from rolling summary + last exchange keeps extractor tokens flat per turn.
  • Zero-LLM read path with a relevance gate (inject nothing below threshold) and a query-length-adaptive dense/BM25 weight.
  • Exact-hash dedup with num_times / date_last_time counters is a cheap first-pass reinforcement signal.
  • Raw turn persistence is synchronous and separate from async derivation, so raw truth survives extraction failure.
avoid
  • Ingest-time dates as 'Stated at' with no event-time field: replayed or imported history loses its timeline (likely cause of T 22.53 in the independent run).
  • Recall reach and normalisation: only the 1,000 most recent embeddings are scanned, BM25 only re-scores dense candidates, and both the BM25 tokeniser and the dedup hash keep ASCII a-z0-9 only, so non-Latin facts collapse into one row.
  • Unbounded history replay: UNIQUE(session_id) means the 30-minute conversation rollover never fires, so BYODB prepends every stored message of the session on every call.
  • Closed hosted extractor with drop-after-retries on failure/quota (content leaves the user's database despite 'BYODB'), and vendor numbers built on precomputed memories with a different embedder and RRF top-10 (81.95-87.0 vs independent 41.34); docs claim 'decay' that is not in the code.

  • nameBYODB on eight SQL/NoSQL dialects without a vector store
    tRaw turns, facts, triples and embeddings live in the user's own SQLite, PostgreSQL/CockroachDB, MySQL/MariaDB, TiDB, Oracle, OceanBase or MongoDB, with embeddings as float32 BLOBs scanned in process; the Rust core reaches every dialect through host-language storage callbacks.

  • namequery-length-adaptive dense/BM25 blend
    tBM25 is computed only over the dense top max(10x limit, 50) pool and blended linearly with cosine; queries of two or fewer content tokens double the lexical weight (0.15 to 0.30), clamped to 0.05-0.40 and env-tunable, implemented identically in Python and Rust with an O(N) partial sort.

  • nameincremental summary-conditioned extraction
    tOnce a conversation summary exists, the Python path sends the hosted extractor only that summary plus the latest user/assistant pair, so extraction input stays flat per turn while the service returns facts, triples and an updated summary in one call.

one_lineTwo-layer episodic + semantic memory library: an LLM groups buffered turns into topic episodes, writes a dated third-person narrative per episode, and distils atomic facts from the gap between a knowledge-based prediction of the episode and the raw turns (predict-calibrate); read is per-layer vector + Postgres full-text fused by RRF.

token_economy
tSmall context comes from two compact layers rather than budgets: k=10 episode narratives (a few sentences each) + 10-20 one-line facts, with raw turns attached only for the top-2 episodes; reported 2,745 tokens per LoCoMo question (88% under full context) and 3.7-4.8K on LongMemEval-S (95-96% under 101K). Write-side economy: episode is the processing unit (one call per episode, not per turn), segmentation batches up to 80 turns per call, and predict-calibrate emits only the novel delta, so fewer and shorter facts. No token budget on the read context, no compression model, no prompt caching; optional total LLM token budget on writes.

speed
tWrite: add returns after durable buffer insert; processing in a background asyncio task, serialised per (agent,user), LLM concurrency 10, embeddings one call per fact (embed_batch exists but is unused), Postgres inserts one row at a time. The README says the Qdrant gRPC client is fully async, but the code uses the synchronous HTTP QdrantClient, which blocks the event loop on every upsert/search. Read: no LLM; episodes and facts searched in parallel; paper: 787 ms search, 3,053 ms end to end with gpt-4o-mini. Anatomy: index construction is token-heavy (7.04M tokens on LoCoMo).

keep
  • Episode as the write unit: one segmentation call per batch of up to 80 turns, then one narrative call per topic episode, instead of per-turn extraction.
  • Predict-calibrate as a dedup-by-construction filter: show the extractor what the store already predicts and keep only the gap (Nemori predicts from episode title + top-k facts, calibrates against raw turns, cold-starts with direct extraction).
  • Two small layers at read time (k=10 dated narratives + 10-20 atomic facts, raw turns only for the top-2 episodes) gives about 2.7K tokens per question with no read-time LLM call.
  • Write absolute dates into episode narratives at write time (relative date rewritten in parentheses), which is where the paper attributes its temporal gains.
  • Per-phase LLM call and token counters plus a hard write token budget in one orchestrator.
avoid
  • Facts are append-only with no supersede or contradiction handling, constant confidence 1.0, and created_at = ingest time shown to the reader as if it were event time.
  • Episode merges delete source episodes and the fact FK is ON DELETE SET NULL, so earlier facts lose provenance; fact-generation failures, single-turn groups (default minimum 2) and turns the segmenter leaves unassigned are dropped while the buffer is deleted anyway.
  • Benchmark hygiene: README 83.05 uses the reader as its own judge with a lenient prompt; an independent rerun scored 0.602-0.781 depending only on judge prompt.
  • Dead config (buffer_size_max, episode_max_messages, both similarity thresholds) and a sync Qdrant client in async code; the LoCoMo harness's one-turn-per-call ingest makes segmentation size timing-dependent.

specialities
  • namePredict-calibrate fact distillation
    tBefore extracting facts, the engine predicts the episode from only its title plus the top-k existing facts, then asks the model to keep only what the raw source turns contain that the prediction missed or got wrong. Known facts are filtered out by construction rather than by a dedup pass; paper v4 credits it with 65.0 vs 52.0 over direct distillation (gpt-4o-mini).
    enemori/llm/generators/semantic.py:77-108; nemori/llm/prompts.py:57-156 (read); arXiv 2508.03341v4 Table 5 (doc)
    phaseextract
  • nameCalibrate against raw turns, not the summary
    tThe calibration step compares the prediction with the verbatim source turns stored on the episode, not with the generated narrative, so narrative omissions do not hide facts; the prediction sees only the title, so it cannot copy the answer.
    enemori/llm/generators/semantic.py:83-101 (read)
    phaseextract
  • nameNon-contiguous topic regrouping
    tOne segmentation call over up to 80 numbered turns returns index lists per topic, and indices may be non-consecutive, so interleaved threads in one chat become separate episodes rather than being cut by position.
    enemori/llm/generators/segmenter.py:15,42-83; nemori/llm/prompts.py:241-308 (read)
    phasesegment
  • nameDated narrative episodes
    tEach episode is a third-person narrative with hour-precise time and relative dates rewritten as absolute dates in parentheses, plus an LLM-inferred event timestamp used as created_at; the paper attributes its temporal gains to this.
    enemori/llm/prompts.py:11-53; nemori/llm/generators/episode.py:63-79 (read)
    phaseextract
  • nameLLM episode consolidation with turn concatenation
    tA new episode is checked against its top-5 vector neighbours and, if the LLM judges it the same event within an hour, both are replaced by one rewritten narrative whose source turns are the concatenation of both, so the episode store stays event-level rather than fragment-level.
    enemori/llm/generators/merger.py:37-171; nemori/core/memory_system.py:132-150 (read)
    phasetime
  • nameZero-LLM two-layer read
    tRead is one query embedding plus per-layer vector and full-text legs fused by RRF, returning two separate top-k lists; the harness attaches raw turns only for the top-2 episodes, giving about 2.7K context tokens per LoCoMo question with no read-time model call.
    enemori/search/unified.py:70-138; evaluation/locomo/search.py:77-94 (read); arXiv 2508.03341v1 Table 2 (doc)
    phaseread
  • namePer-phase LLM accounting with hard budget
    tEvery write-time call goes through one orchestrator that tags it by phase, counts calls and tokens per phase, caps concurrency and can stop all extraction once a token budget is spent.
    enemori/llm/orchestrator.py:72-157; nemori/core/memory_system.py:231-251 (read)
    phasecost
  • nameDistillation kernel for other engines
    tPaper v4 reframes predict-calibrate as a front-end usable before other memory managers (A-MEM, MemoryOS), reporting 45-64% less stored text; no such adapter exists in the repo.
    earXiv 2508.03341v4 Table 7 (doc)
    phaseextract

token_economy
tThree levers. (1) Compress before any LLM sees text: LLMLingua-2 drops 20-40% of tokens per message locally. (2) Batch extraction: turns accumulate to a 512-1,024 token sensory buffer, are cut by topic, and a 512-token short-term buffer is flushed as one JSON-mode call, so LoCoMo needs about 255-415 write calls in total versus about 5.5-19k for MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0 in the same table; memory construction is 0.76-1.0M tokens versus 2.9-68M for the baselines. (3) Move consolidation offline: the update pass costs only 39-64k tokens on LoCoMo with gpt-4o-mini (55-107k with qwen3) because the queue is built by vector search and only pairs above 0.9 similarity reach the LLM. Read side stays plain: top-60 single-line facts, about 2,600 prompt tokens per question (full text about 35,600). Paper abstract (arXiv 2510.18866, latest version): on LongMemEval / LoCoMo up to 7.7% / 29.3% accuracy gain, 38x / 20.9x lower total tokens, 30x / 55.5x fewer API calls; online test-time only, 106x / 117x fewer tokens and 159x / 310x fewer calls. These ratios are against the vendor's own baseline runs, including a weak Mem0 (36.49).
epre_compressor/llmlingua_2.py:54-89; short_term_memory.py:36-57; lightmem.py:173, 459-644; experiments/locomo/readme.md; README.md:391-400; arXiv 2510.18866 abstract [read+doc]
speed
tWrite: extraction calls run in a ThreadPoolExecutor (max 5); the LoCoMo harness processes conversations in a process pool of 5 with one API key each. Offline queue construction uses 8 threads and the update 5 threads, guarded by locks, but each entry's candidate lookup scans every other entry's queue, so the update pass is quadratic in store size; worker exceptions are never collected from executor.map. Compression, segmentation and embedding are local GPU models, so no network cost there, but each turn is embedded one at a time during segmentation and each fact is embedded and inserted one at a time (no batching). Nothing is async and add_memory blocks for the LLM call when a buffer flushes. Published runtimes on LoCoMo: 7,388-8,484 s memory construction and about 4,300 s QA in total for 10 conversations with gpt-4o-mini, versus 24k-118k s construction for MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0 in the same table. No per-query latency percentiles published.

keep
  • Local token-classifier compression (LLMLingua-2) before the extractor: cheap, model-free of the hosted LLM, and the same encoder doubles as the topic segmenter.
  • Buffer-and-batch extraction: segment by topic, then pack several segments into one token-capped extraction call (one call per about 500 tokens of user text rather than per turn).
  • Sleep-time consolidation off the write path, gated by vector similarity (only pairs above about 0.9 reach the LLM) and restricted to earlier entries, so update cost stays tiny.
  • Per-stage token/call/runtime accounting built into the engine, and reporting cost tables next to accuracy.
  • Timestamp plus weekday prefix on every retrieved fact so the reader can resolve relative dates cheaply.
avoid
  • Undurable receipt: turns sit in in-process buffers until a flush, global topic and summary counters are module-level, extraction errors are swallowed, and a non-on_disk local Qdrant store (the default) is deleted at construction, so a crash, failed call or restart silently loses memory.
  • Offline update rewrites fact text but keeps the old embedding, hard-deletes on conflict with no history, and summaries are not refreshed when covered facts change.
  • Declared-but-dead features: online update is a no-op, BM25/context retrieval is an empty file, graph_mem crashes, kv_cache/history_db/extract_threshold unused, offline_update_trigger raises TypeError (PR #80).
  • No tenant ids, auth, firewall or redaction, and TLS verification is disabled in the OpenAI client; user_only default drops everything the assistant says.

specialities
  • nameOne small encoder for compression and segmentation
    tThe LLMLingua-2 BERT-base token classifier drops 20-40% of tokens per message, and with precomp_topic_shared the same weights supply the attention maps for topic boundaries, so both write-side token cuts run on one local model before any hosted LLM call.
    efactory/pre_compressor/llmlingua_2.py:54-89; topic_segmenter/llmlingua_2.py:9-21, 25-120; lightmem.py:164-170 [read]
    phasesegment
  • nameAttention-plus-embedding topic boundaries
    tCoarse cuts are local maxima of turn-to-previous-turn attention from encoder layers 8-11; fine cuts are adjacent-turn cosine dips with an adaptive threshold (0.2 rising to 0.5); fine cuts are kept only within 3 turns of a coarse cut. No LLM is used for segmentation.
    etopic_segmenter/llmlingua_2.py:25-120; sensory_memory.py:54-141 [read]
    phasesegment
  • nameToken-capped multi-topic extraction batches
    tTopic segments accumulate in a 512-token short-term buffer and are flushed as one JSON-mode call with '--- Topic N ---' sections, so the whole LoCoMo set needs 255-415 write-side LLM calls versus about 5.5-19k for MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0 in the vendor's tables.
    eshort_term_memory.py:36-57; openai.py:315-346; experiments/locomo/readme.md:117-121; README.md:389-397 [read + doc]
    phaseextract
  • nameTime-directed, similarity-gated sleep-time update
    tEach fact's update queue holds its top 10 of 20 nearest neighbours with earlier-or-equal timestamps; only pairs above 0.9 cosine reach the update/delete/ignore LLM, run offline in parallel. The whole LoCoMo update cost 39-64k tokens with gpt-4o-mini.
    elightmem.py:459-644; prompts.py:334-406; add_locomo.py:446-447; experiments/locomo/readme.md:136-140 [read + doc]
    phasetime
  • nameTimestamp-keyed event reconstruction
    tAll facts extracted from one message share its millisecond timestamp, so StructMem treats the timestamp as an implicit event key: each semantically retrieved seed pulls in its same-timestamp siblings before cross-event summarisation.
    eutils.py:60-111, 313-317, 443-466 [read]
    phasederive
  • namePer-stage cost ledger in the engine
    tLightMemory counts calls and prompt/completion tokens separately for add, update and summarise, plus embedder calls, and exposes them via get_token_statistics(); the vendor publishes cost and runtime tables alongside accuracy.
    elightmem.py:143-160, 711-750; experiments/locomo/readme.md:113-148 [read + doc]
    phaseeval
  • nameBoundMem tags carried inside memory text
    tOptional environment tags are written as a JSON prefix inside the memory string, so they survive any store or export, are stripped before embedding and before display, and drive a hard or pluggable soft tag-overlap filter at read.
    elightmem.py:375-380, 413-415, 684-703; utils.py:757-966 [read]
    phaseread

token_economy
tEach memory is a 15-80 word fact; OSS search defaults to top_k 20 (roughly 0.4k-2k tokens), while vendor runs use top_200 at a mean of 6,956 tokens on LoCoMo (91.8 vs 92.5 at top_50). speed
tRead: zero LLM; entity-store searches run on a 4-thread pool; one query embedding plus one batch for entities. Write: one LLM call, batch embeddings, bulk insert. token_economy
tEpisodes replace raw turns as the retrieved unit: EverAlgo's committed agentic runs inject 2,294-2,596 tokens per question for top 10; the EverOS 94.42 run injects top 20 (not measured), and the cloud measured 8,559. HEAD caps the summary at about 50 words / 400 width units with a 3-tier repair. Embeddings are MRL-truncated to 1,024-d. The read side is heavy: EverAlgo agentic search used about 2.8k prompt tokens per question, and llm_multiround with full_text reads up to 50 full episodes in round 0.

speed
tEpisode written inline before /add returns; facts, profile and index built in background (OME + cascade daemon; docs say sub-second, up to about 10-15 s under load); per-session locks with 360 s timeout; per-owner partition locks for profile; embedding batches of 10 with 5 concurrent; episode body and subject embedded concurrently; search legs run under asyncio.gather. EverAlgo's LoCoMo profile: extraction 1,348 s, search 1,280 s, answer 912 s for the whole set at 10 conversations in parallel.

All-question audit crosswalk

The 25 historical hypotheses below remain linked to the frozen 2,399-question audit. Do not reinterpret rule matches as confirmed root causes. V01/V02 match all questions because they are universal validation checks, not because every question has a defect. The 57,204 saved cells retain original answers/gold/scores; this review does not relabel them from memory.

Source drift: the current forensics_explorer.html differs from the frozen audit hash. The historical validator reached and passed the 2,399-question / 57,204-cell equality assertions, then failed its source-HTML hash check. This is not a fresh all-question audit of the changed explorer. Preserve the frozen records; inventory and adjudicate the changed source separately.

Every-question hypothesis matrix · Earlier gap register

M01 · Use finalized, explicit scoring contracts

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idM01
titleUse finalized, explicit scoring contracts
problemThe explorer reads provisional repetition scores from results.jsonl. A positive score can also coexist with a truncated answer.
proposalUse finalized OP-Bench per_probe scores when available; retain provisional values and their basis. Require completed, nonempty answers for answer-pass diagnostics. Keep retrieval-only, missing, pending and failed states separate. Report official OP-Bench task/person macro scores separately from pass@0.5.
regression_riskChanging display semantics can look like model regression; changing the benchmark formula would invalidate comparisons.
acceptance_testRebuild from unchanged files: official macro must stay identical; provisional/final differences must be visible; first repetition answer must not automatically count as a final success; truncated and retrieval-only rows must not silently count as correct/incorrect answers.

M02 · Validate evidence references and isolate annotation disputes

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idM02
titleValidate evidence references and isolate annotation disputes
problemEight raw evidence references are malformed or unresolved. Other labels conflict with source dates, speakers or predicates.
proposalAdd a reversible evidence-normalization view with raw and resolved IDs, missing-reference errors and adjudication status. Keep official labels immutable. Report official score and a separately versioned adjudicated diagnostic; never silently train retrieval toward a known wrong label.
regression_riskOverzealous repair can join different turns or reinterpret a genuinely incorrect answer as a gold error.
acceptance_testEvery repaired reference must resolve within the same conversation; orphan/missing IDs remain unresolved. Adjudication requires an exact source span and independent review. Test wrong speaker, absent image content, dates and answer-list supersets.

R01 · Recover evidence through bounded, intent-specific search

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idR01
titleRecover evidence through bounded, intent-specific search
problemA relevant instance can be absent from the logged semantic/lexical candidates, especially for lists, category-to-instance queries and multi-hop relations.
proposalClassify the required answer shape and unresolved relations; issue a bounded second retrieval only for missing evidence slots. Use independent lexical and semantic paths, entity aliases with provenance, and one-hop relation expansion. Stop at a fixed cost cap or when slots are supported.
regression_riskQuery expansion introduces plausible but irrelevant facts, increases latency and can amplify a wrong entity assumption.
acceptance_testMeasure evidence recall, answer precision and cost together. Include entity-swapped, irrelevant-memory and unanswerable controls. Compare no/single/multi retrieval at the same total budget; do not trigger on benchmark IDs or names.

R02 · Preserve independent evidence under a fixed candidate budget

Current-status overlay: PARTIAL / BUILT-OFF hooks exist; see RV16. Full hypothesis is not proven implemented or effective.

idR02
titlePreserve independent evidence under a fixed candidate budget
problemGold evidence can enter a retrieval leg but disappear during fusion, pool cutting or reranking. The perspective leg filters vector hits and is not independent evidence.
proposalReserve bounded candidate shares for independent source families; deduplicate correlated vector/perspective votes. Apply hard namespace, deletion and trust filters before admission. Rerank a fixed-size diverse pool with compact relation context. Protect evidence coverage, not every high-ranking noisy hit.
regression_riskRaw per-leg protection can enlarge the pool and increase cost; noisy lexical hits can displace strong semantic hits. Existing balanced selection already trades categories.
acceptance_testLog leg→pool→rerank→context transitions with cap metadata. Compare at fixed pool/context limits. Check single-hop, multi-hop, temporal and OP-Bench separately, with paired gains/losses. No adoption from net score alone.

R03 · Select evidence bundles and account for the real prompt budget

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idR03
titleSelect evidence bundles and account for the real prompt budget
problemA hit can survive ranking but lose its antecedent, question, or source during window assembly; overlapping windows waste tokens.
proposalRepresent minimal evidence bundles containing claim, speaker, antecedent and time anchor. Merge overlapping windows and allocate an explicit prompt budget including headers and answer reserve. Preserve source boundaries and log what was dropped. Test evidence placement instead of assuming more context helps.
regression_riskExtra neighbors introduce distractors or another speaker’s facts; overcompression removes a qualifier; exact provider tokenization can add overhead.
acceptance_testBudget-boundary tests must retain complete supported bundles or report insufficient evidence. Vary distractor count and evidence position while holding content fixed; verify context/output limits and latency.

A01 · Bind every claim to its subject, speaker and modality

Current-status overlay: PARTIAL / BUILT-OFF hooks exist; see RV16. Full hypothesis is not proven implemented or effective.

idA01
titleBind every claim to its subject, speaker and modality
problemA statement by one participant is assigned to another; a reply contains evidence about the question’s subject but a speaker-only filter discards it.
proposalKeep speaker, addressee, described subject, assertion source and modality as distinct fields. Bind extracted claims to these fields and retain original spans. Resolve short replies through a bounded dialogue edge. Use uncertainty rather than globally treating speaker=subject or accepting a name as a relevance bypass.
regression_riskHard speaker filters lose statements about another participant; guessed coreference can create persistent false facts.
acceptance_testSwap names and speaker order; factual answers should change only with subject ownership. Test replies, quotations, pronouns, assistant-owned claims, third-party queries and same-name users. Never cross namespaces.

A02 · Separate event state, identity and time

Current-status overlay: PARTIAL / BUILT-OFF hooks exist; see RV16. Full hypothesis is not proven implemented or effective.

idA02
titleSeparate event state, identity and time
problemPlans, recommendations, completed events, repeated mentions and historical changes are conflated.
proposalUse source-backed event tuples: actor, action, object, location, event-time interval, mention time, status and provenance. Link repeated mentions only when enough identity evidence agrees. Preserve updates and contradictions; answer according to the requested time and completion predicate.
regression_riskAggressive event merging undercounts; treating every mention as a distinct event overcounts; latest-only truth loses history.
acceptance_testTest planned→cancelled→completed transitions, two same-day events, one event mentioned on two days, conflicting reports, residence versus visit, pregnancy versus birth, and recommendation versus purchase.

A03 · Carry the requested answer type through retrieval and generation

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idA03
titleCarry the requested answer type through retrieval and generation
problemAnswers return countries for a city question, dates for a title question, or related facts that do not satisfy the requested predicate.
proposalBuild a small typed query contract: target subject, relation, answer type, time scope and expected cardinality. Retrieve against the contract, then verify each final claim matches it. Use trusted external knowledge only when the question permits it and mark that provenance separately.
regression_riskA rigid classifier can misroute ambiguous questions or reject useful qualified answers.
acceptance_testTest cities/countries, author/composer, visits/residence, winner/participant, support/endorsement and literal versus hypothetical questions. Uncertain classification should fall back to a general evidence-grounded path.

A04 · Evaluate lists for both completeness and precision

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idA04
titleEvaluate lists for both completeness and precision
problemA response may contain the gold item yet add unsupported items, or receive credit for a partial list.
proposalBuild an evidence table with one row per candidate item, its supporting turn and predicate match. Deduplicate by entity/event identity. Return supported items and an explicit completeness qualification if coverage is uncertain. Score item recall and unsupported-item rate separately.
regression_riskRetrieving more candidates increases false positives; a verifier can reject legitimate paraphrases or collapse distinct items.
acceptance_testTest partial lists, correct supersets with irrelevant additions, similar names, repeated mentions and other-speaker items. A gain requires improved supported coverage without increased unsupported items, not mere gold-string inclusion.

A05 · Compute dates from source-bound intervals

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idA05
titleCompute dates from source-bound intervals
problemRelative dates, duration arithmetic and weekday annotations are inconsistent; mention time is mistaken for event time.
proposalParse supported expressions into date/interval operands bound to a specific turn and event. Run fixed trusted arithmetic for differences and calendar operations. Preserve approximate intervals and unresolved ambiguity; render an exact day only when supported. Resolve conflicting weekday/date assertions explicitly.
regression_riskPicking an unrelated timestamp silently produces a precise wrong answer; deterministic computation cannot repair an unsupported operand.
acceptance_testCover month/year boundaries, leap years, next/last weekday, vague other-day/last-week phrases, conflicting anchors, incomplete events and inclusive/exclusive duration conventions. Verify operands and precision as well as result.

A06 · Count supported events rather than mentions

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idA06
titleCount supported events rather than mentions
problemLexical/date deduplication does not establish event identity, completion or the requested predicate.
proposalConstruct a small provenance-linked ledger for the query and count only distinct entries that satisfy the actor, action, status and time constraints. Reconcile explicit cumulative counts against the ledger; if the evidence conflicts, return a range or explain the unresolved count.
regression_riskSame-day token overlap can merge different events; repeated mentions on different dates can be double-counted; ordinal wins are not total participations.
acceptance_testTest repeated mentions, same-day separate visits, scheduled versus completed trips, winners versus entries, two participants, explicit ordinals and uncertain dates. Verify each counted item can be inspected.

A07 · Recover referents without inventing multimodal evidence

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idA07
titleRecover referents without inventing multimodal evidence
problemThis, that, we and image references need adjacent context; text captions may omit the title, place or object required by gold.
proposalAttach explicit reply/reference edges and bounded neighbor context. Record whether an image was actually available and what text/caption/OCR supports. If visual evidence is missing, mark the question unsupported under the text-only protocol rather than guessing a familiar place or object.

acceptance_testTest shuffled neighbors, ambiguous photos, misleading captions and missing images. Compare text-only and multimodal arms separately with fixed inputs. No credit for guessing an unobservable label.

A08 · Separate supported facts, hypotheses and recommendations

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idA08
titleSeparate supported facts, hypotheses and recommendations
problemOpen-domain gold sometimes requires a non-unique recommendation or an unsupported inference about age, health, religion, wealth or residence.
proposalLabel requested behavior as factual recall, grounded inference or recommendation. State a hypothesis with its uncertainty when invited; do not promote it into a stored user fact. Allow multiple evidence-consistent recommendations. For personal attributes without support, preserve unknown.
regression_riskOverabstention damages useful advice; optimizing one speculative gold answer encourages stereotyping and false memories.
acceptance_testUse paired factual/hypothetical prompts and unsupported-attribute controls. Judge support and usefulness separately. A recommendation may be useful without being a unique gold fact; it must not become asserted history.

P01 · Condition memory use on current intent and target subject

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idP01
titleCondition memory use on current intent and target subject
problemGeneric requests receive unrelated personal facts; broad filtering also damages valid LoCoMo recall.
proposalEstimate whether memory can supply a required answer slot, then filter candidate claims for subject and intent relevance. Permit an empty memory context when none helps. Preserve relevant negative constraints and third-party references. Treat direct personal recall as a strong feature, not a universal name/first-person bypass.

acceptance_testPair generic and personal variants of the same request, including pronouns, names, third parties and multi-hop facts. Measure OP-Bench official macro plus LoCoMo paired losses, relevant-constraint retention, latency and refusal rate.

P02 · Reduce repeated persona insertion without chasing word diversity

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idP02
titleReduce repeated persona insertion without chasing word diversity
problemThe same personal themes recur across unrelated responses; different wording can hide the same irrelevant personalization.
proposalTrack which persona claims were recently used and require a current-task reason to reuse them. Prefer the answer’s actual topic. Evaluate both repeated themes and factual usefulness, keeping essential repeated constraints such as allergies when relevant.
regression_riskA novelty objective can omit necessary facts or invent new ones; evaluation-wide state can leak future answers into generation.
acceptance_testUse chronological, per-user state only. Test recurring relevant constraints, unrelated topic sequences and identity isolation. Report official final repetition score with human/claim-level relevance checks; no tuning solely to lexical similarity.

P03 · Check assertions before agreeing with the user

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idP03
titleCheck assertions before agreeing with the user
problemThe assistant accepts false remembered events or preferences and confuses conversational friendliness with factual agreement.
proposalCompare the user assertion with source-backed facts; distinguish confirmed, contradicted and unknown. Correct only the factual premise while answering the useful part of the request. Keep values and preferences separate from objective claims and do not invent personal history.
regression_riskBlanket disagreement harms legitimate preferences and corrections; absence from memory does not prove an event never happened.
acceptance_testTest true/false/unknown assertions with equivalent tone, supplied user corrections and value disagreements. Score factual agreement, unsupported history, helpfulness and irrelevant memory use independently.

G01 · Verify answer support before limited retries

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idG01
titleVerify answer support before limited retries
problemEvidence is present but the answer is wrong, overlong, contradictory or an unjustified refusal.
proposalUse an answer contract with source-linked claims and a compact final response. Run a bounded check for unsupported claims, missing requested slots, operand/result consistency and completion. Retry only a diagnosed failure using the same evidence or a targeted missing-evidence request.
regression_riskRetries increase cost and can turn a correct abstention into a hallucination; a verifier correlated with the reader may repeat its error.
acceptance_testCompare first and final answers, retry reason and acceptance. Test answerable and unanswerable cases, long reasoning, arithmetic contradictions and misleading context. Require improvement in supported answers at a bounded cost.

E02 · Run a bounded loop driven by missing evidence

Current-status overlay: Historical proposal; current implementation not independently certified here.

idE02
titleRun a bounded loop driven by missing evidence
problemAn action loop that selects a tool for a specific unresolved slot will outperform blind answer retries at a comparable total cost.
proposalAfter each evidence assessment, choose one action: memory search, relation expansion, neighbor lookup, asset inspection, public-knowledge lookup, deterministic calculation, answer or qualified stop. Each action names the missing slot. Stop on sufficiency, exhausted budget, repeated action, no new useful evidence or an unresolved contradiction. Build on the existing agentic read rather than introducing another unbounded loop.

problemOriginal-asset OCR or vision will recover entity labels omitted by generic captions, enabling reliable joins between visual identity and textual event time.

statusPROPOSED refinement of existing families; not implemented or validated

Claude second opinions and adjudication

Two read-only Claude Code reviews were requested using Read/Glob/Grep. Reports are independent reviewer opinions, not authority. Their evidence and limitations are preserved. Review RV01 rejects exactly-once inference wording; RV02 rejects rigid literal span rules; RV04 rejects universal utterance-time ordering; RV12 rejects a guaranteed-zero-false-positive seed gate. RV19 rejects always retrying a valid empty extraction. RV18 qualifies the survey reviewer’s text-identity shorthand for Graphiti, which also performs semantic resolution. RV20 retains Mnemon’s zero-LLM record-write distinction.

Record / findingFull evidence, assessment and proposed solution
engine review · 18 findings
summaryReview of the MemSpine snapshot on branch feat/local-qwen-stack (HEAD 2df543d; the brief says 2f9c3e4, and G-W50 and G-E1 landed after it). I found no G-W49 code in the tree. It is a proposal in gap_plan.json:540-551, the Codex brief and prompt v2. The existing window write (workers/windows.py, core/window.py) is built but opt-in (schema.py:1757 default 'off'). The direction of G-W49 is plausible. Several load-bearing claims are unsupported, internally contradicted, or depend on infrastructure that does not exist. (1) The speed case rests on prompt size and on a latency ratio that does not fit the source study. (2) The online deposit cannot reuse `emit` as it is. (3) Durability is weaker than 'retry-safe' wording suggests. Some forget and cache paths also depend on in-process state. (4) Span grounding is a weak check. (5) The earlier deep_audit hypothesis docs apply a blanket 'not implemented' status to capabilities that exist. They also report regex-generated applicability decisions as 'exhaustive review'. Nothing was executed. No result files, credentials or settings were read.

    correctionG-W45 (prefill about 10%) undercuts G-W49's speed argument. The gain is mostly output tokens (one item list instead of facts plus edges, no speaker, subject, persons, location, topic or confidence). The 309 figure belongs to a superseded draft. The 958 figure has no recorded method.
    proposed_generic_solutionReport tokens per call by role from the tokenizer actually served: static prefix, variable input, completion. Rank cost by completion tokens times decode speed plus uncached prefill. Pin the prompt hash with its measured count.
    validation_gateA manifest records prompt hash, tokenizer, static and variable tokens, completion tokens and wall time per call for both arms on the same windows. The ≥30% gate is on completion tokens and p50 latency, with prefix-cache state recorded.

G-W49 therefore relies on the model's KNOWN-name reuse (rule 6) for the common case, which is unverified. G-W29 uses a different 0.9 (embedding similarity, gap_plan.json:157), also uncalibrated. The two thresholds are easy to confuse in the docs.
    proposed_generic_solutionName the thresholds by what they measure. Calibrate each on a labelled set of same and different entity pairs from unrelated domains. Refresh the known-entity table after each deposit so names are resolved against earlier batches.
    validation_gatePairwise precision and recall of rules-mode resolution on a held-out entity-pair set, reported per length bucket. A duplicate-entity rate over a long stream is tracked between sleeps.

  • claude-sonnet-5-5
survey review · 17 findings
summaryStructure is complete: all 15 records have 57 rows and 15 layers, and the prompt matrix has 345 cells (15 × 23). Evidence tags are mostly explicit, but only at row level. The genuine-evidence problems are in the synthesis, the gap plan and the builders. I re-checked about 20 high-consequence claims in source. Most record-level facts held: Mem0 keeps deleted text in history, MemMachine profile facts survive source deletion, Hindsight deletes cascade to observations, Cognee's per-turn analysis call is on by default, and Honcho's dream thresholds match. The weak points are generalizations built on top of the records. The main ones: 'lose turns on failed extraction' (Nemori, MemOS), 'small contexts come from a hard budget', the Graphiti call and identity description in G-W49/G-W50, 'example-free' prompts, the 60/20/10/10 shares, and 'wave A needs no screen'. The builders also show a vendor LoCoMo number under each engine that can describe different code, a different version, or a different harness than the cells below it. The SPEC has no status for closed, hosted or legacy, so N conflates 'absent' with 'not inspectable'. All conclusions are pinned to the local snapshots; none were run.

coverage_limitations
  • I did not read every line. Most rows of the 15 records were not individually re-verified; what I report is a prioritised sample (truth/durability, deletion, scope, defaults, cost, and cross-document generalizations).
  • Several long cells are shown as 'Omitted long line' by the search tool and were not read in full (e.g. memos extract.calls and extract.failure text, memori rows 26/31/58/59/62, hindsight and lightmem token_economy text).
  • No engine outside Graphiti, Mem0, MemOS, Nemori, MemMachine, EverMemOS, Cognee, Honcho, Hindsight, MIRIX and MemSpine was source-rechecked. Mnemon, memU, LightMem, Memori and the Combined engine were audited from their records only (Mnemon, memU and Memori cross-checked against the matrix and gap text).
  • I did not verify any LoCoMo number, hosted-cloud behaviour, or the 'our notes' figures. Nothing was run, and Mnemon's hosted decision model cannot be read from the repo.
  • The prompt-matrix scores were checked only for structure, variant handling, and the F18 column. The F1-F23 judgements for most engines were not re-derived.
  • Graphiti was read at 0.31.0 / 964bb11 only. The vendored copy under combined-src is an older version and was not diffed against it.
  • MemSpine own-code checks covered the cited G-W25, G-W27, G-W50, G-P6 and default-auth claims. The other 'now' corrections (15 reported) were not re-checked, nor was the claimed 958-token / 309-token prompt sizes.
  • The EverMemOS cross-project overwrite and the Nemori one-message-batch loss under the LoCoMo harness settings were not traced to the end.

  • synthesis.json: rewrite the 'hard budget' bullet (F-03), the 'never per turn' bullet (F-09), the 'lose turns' bullets (F-02) and the 'no LLM on read' bullet (F-13). Label the section 3 shares as an untested hypothesis. Remove engine names from the Source column of the shares table.

  • build_comparison.py: pick the header score by applies_to=pinned_commit, not by list order; fail the build on JSON load errors, a missing row or layer, an untagged `e`, or a status outside Y/O/P/N/U; stop hiding 'see engine document'; derive the lede counts from data and state the actual selection method.

  • Add reusable MemSpine gap rows (no leaderboard): derivation-failure taxonomy and tests (F-02); full-path token ledger per stage (F-03); block-shares sweep with quote-question non-inferiority (F-04); idempotency key vs identity separation plus provenance-on-archived fix (F-10); two-tenant isolation test matrix (F-11); erasure cascade scan (F-12); gate-fired counters in screens (F-16); record linter (F-17).

Reproducibility and limitations

Local code pointers above are relative to src/memspine unless docs/evals is stated. All input hashes and local clone heads are in manifest.json. Structural checks are in validation.json.
